ideas.title: Alpine Mind — performance coaching for amateur alpine athletes
ideas.oneLiner: Blended mental + physical performance coaching for serious amateur skiers and sliding-sport athletes — online programme with premium in-person camps.

market.why: Global ski/snowsports participation is large but the 'serious amateur willing to pay for coaching' slice is a niche; sliding sports (skeleton/luge) are tiny. Real TAM sizing needed before committing.

entry.why: Low regulatory barrier; can launch with a landing page, a coaching curriculum and a booking calendar. Credibility is the main gate, which the team can supply.

cost.why: Digital-first keeps startup cost low (sub-CAD $20k to a paid pilot). In-person camps add cost but only once demand is proven.

saturation.why: General online fitness coaching is crowded; alpine-specific + sport-psychology positioning is far less contested. Differentiation carries the score.

moat.why: Moat is credibility + proprietary curriculum + community, not technology. Defensible if a brand and results are built early, weak otherwise.

margins.why: Digital coaching margins are high; camps are lower-margin but strong for brand and lifetime value. Blended margin attractive.

founderFit.why: Unusually strong: the team combines elite alpine/sliding-sport experience, sport-psychology depth, and business/finance skills — a rare, credible pairing for exactly this niche.

risk.why: Main risks are niche demand and founder time (part-time, distributed team). Low capital-at-risk keeps downside contained.

businessCase.summary: A premium coaching brand for amateur alpine athletes who want to get measurably better — pairing physical technique with the mental/psychology side that most coaching ignores. Recurring online revenue, with high-margin in-person camps as the flagship experience and brand engine.
businessCase.customer: Serious amateur skiers, ski-racers, and sliding-sport athletes (25–55) who already spend on gear, travel and lift passes and are frustrated by plateauing performance.
businessCase.market: Snowsports participation is large and affluent; the paid-coaching and performance-camp segment is smaller but high-value. This needs real sizing — flagged low-confidence until researched.
businessCase.model: Tiered subscription for the online programme (technique library, structured plans, mental-performance modules, group calls) + paid seasonal in-person camps + 1:1 upsell.
businessCase.goToMarket: Founder credibility and content marketing (social + YouTube), partnerships with clubs and resorts, and camps as a high-touch acquisition funnel.
businessCase.costs: Curriculum production, video, coaching time, a booking/community platform, and camp logistics. Low fixed cost until camps scale.
businessCase.risks: Niche demand ceiling; seasonality; reliance on part-time founder attention; brand depends on demonstrable athlete results.
businessCase.nextSteps: Validate willingness-to-pay with 20 target athletes; size the paid-coaching segment properly; run one small paid pilot cohort before building anything.

clarifyingQuestions: Which segment leads — mainstream skiers (bigger market) or sliding sports (tiny but uniquely defensible for this team)?
Online-first with camps as upsell, or camps-first with online as retention?
Which geographies for the first camps, and who owns delivery given the team is distributed?
